text:
jess: heads-up — Greenline (customer) reports webhooks failing since ~10:12 UTC after our scheduled networking maintenance. They see 403 from their firewall and say their allowlist still lists our old egress IPs. Ticket #GL-4823 attached.

matt: can you paste the source IP the customer is seeing in their logs?

jess: customer sent this: `source_ip=34.88.120.45` and `x-request-id=gl-req-7c9a`. They also included snippet: `curl -i https://hooks.greenline.co/payload -H 'X-Redwood-Request: gl-req-7c9a'` -> `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` from their edge.

priya: @jess thanks. Do we have any NAT rotation events around 10:00-10:20 UTC for their VPC/account? Also ask customer to verify there are no additional proxies rewriting src IPs.

samir: I kicked off a quick audit — we did a SNAT rebind for the private VPC pool in us-west-2 as part of autoscale maintenance at 10:08 UTC. The job rotated ephemeral egress addresses on nat-pool-7 to balance utilization. Looks like greenline's allowlist still has the previous allocation.

infra-bot: [notice] NAT rotate job completed: nat-rotate-2026-04-12-1005 — affected pools: nat-pool-7 (us-west-2). New allocation IDs: alloc-9c2, alloc-9d3.

jess: customer says they maintain a strict allowlist and cannot accept frequent IP churn. Asking for a workaround — can we restore previous mapping short-term or give them a static egress option?

matt: short-term we can attempt to reprovision the old egress block back onto the pool, but that may impact capacity. Alternative: give the customer the new IPs to update their firewall (list below). New egress seen from our side: `34.88.120.45`, `34.88.120.46`, `34.88.120.47`.

priya: jess, please send the customer the three new IPs and ask them to whitelist. Also, request a sample `tcpdump`/`curl -v` output showing the 403 if they can.

greenline-agent: thanks — we updated allowlist with the three IPs you provided and retried. Still getting 403s. We also see TLS handshake successes then immediate 403 from our firewall appliance. Here's partial `curl -v`:

```
* Connected to hooks.greenline.co (34.88.120.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.3 connection established
> GET /payload HTTP/1.1
> Host: hooks.greenline.co
> X-Redwood-Request: gl-req-7c9a
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< Content-Type: text/plain
< X-Edge-Decision: blocked-by-firewall
```

priya: odd — if TLS succeeds but their firewall still blocks, either they have additional application-layer allowlist/ACLs keyed on something else (eg client ASN, certs) or there's caching on their firewall. @matt any chance their allowlist appliance cached the old mapping (DNS or IP) with a long TTL and still enforcing a previous deny rule?

matt: their firewall message `blocked-by-firewall` looks internal to them. I ran `dig +short hooks.greenline.co` from our egress and got `34.88.120.45` — DNS resolves fine. On our side the L4/L7 handoff looks normal. Could you ask them to flush any proxy caches or check the appliance rule matching (IP vs netblock vs security tag)?

jess: customer says they use a third-party appliance (ApplGuard 5K) with an implicit rule that blocks any new IPs unless pulled from an enterprise MC list. They're escalating internally but want us to avoid future churn. They asked whether we can pin an egress IP for their private deployment.

samir: we can create a reserved egress allocation for their VPC (requires Dedicated/Private plan add-on). Quick mitigation: I just attempted a rollback to the previous allocation mapping for nat-pool-7 — rollback failed due to collision with active allocation for another customer. Rolling that back is unsafe.

priya: action items: (1) jess send new IP list and request appliance cache flush + rule check; (2) samir file request for reserved egress (ops ticket OP-9812) and estimate lead time; (3) matt monitor logs for requests with `x-request-id=gl-req-7c9a` and confirm whether any 2xx responses reached greenline during the window.

matt: monitoring now. I see repeated 403 responses from 10:12–10:26 UTC with identical X-Edge-Decision header. No successful deliveries.

infra-bot: [alert] NAT rebinds scheduled: nat-pool-7 will continue to rotate under current autoscale policy. To prevent churn, set `egress.reserved=true` on the VPC or open a reserved allocation ticket.

greenline-agent: we've flushed the appliance cache and retried — still 403. We can open an enterprise support request but need a timeline. Can you provide ETA for reserved egress? We cannot keep updating the allowlist every maintenance window.

jess: explained that reserved egress setup takes ~2-3 business days pending approvals; meanwhile we escalated to eng-sre for emergency exception. Apologies for the impact.

samir: created OP-9812 and linked customer: requested manual allocation of a /29 from our reserved pool for Greenline VPC. I've also added a temporary rule in our routing plane to prefer that allocation for their account. Changes applied — please test.

greenline-agent: after your change we retried — webhooks are now accepted 🎉. Firewall logs show requests from 203.0.113.200 (the reserved IP) and accepted. Thank you. Can we get this documented in the ticket as a permanent config?

priya: filed follow-up doc in the ticket: summary, root cause = autoscale-driven SNAT rebind combined with customer's strict appliance rules; mitigation = reserved egress allocation + ops guidance. Recommend we add a support KB for customers on allowlist-sensitive deployments.

jess: closing loop with customer and asking product to surface reserved-egress as an option during onboarding for Private customers.

matt: follow-up: propose adding telemetry to alert when a VPC's egress IP block changes and the customer has enterprise allowlist flag set — would prevent silent failures. Filing feature request: FR-2026-278.

samir: noted. I'll also add a guard to avoid rotating allocations that are pinned in the last 30 days for accounts flagged as \"allowlist-sensitive\".

jess: thanks everyone. GL confirmed stable and ticket will be closed after we publish KB. :white_check_mark:
